 South African Enters FIFA Presidential Race
 Nov 16, 2026 - 02:53 pm
 By SL Staff Reporter
 Add to Preferred Sources 
 Peter Auf der Heyde is seeking to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in 2027.Photo by Mahugnon Leopold Soglo/Gallo Images
 South African-German journalist Peter Auf der Heyde is seeking to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in 2027, with a campaign centred on greater transparency, accountability and representation for smaller football nations. 
 Every Nation Matters Campaign 
 Check Out: Benni Explains Bafana's Striker Problem, Backs Foster 
 Auf der Heyde, who has almost five decades of involvement in football as a player, administrator, club manager, journalist and academic, has launched his campaign under the banner Every Nation Matters. 
 He is seeking five nominations from FIFA's 211 member associations to become an official candidate, with his proposals including an Emerging Nations World Cup, an independent Football Advisory Council and greater investment in women's football. 
 He has also pledged to accept only US$1 annually in presidential remuneration unless independently assessed campaign promises are fulfilled. 
 However, his challenge to Infantino has already raised questions about the incumbent's eligibility to seek another term. 
 Candidate Questions Infantino's Eligibility 
 Article 33(2) of the FIFA Statutes limits the president to three terms, consecutive or otherwise. Infantino was elected in 2016, 2019 and 2023, but FIFA adopted an interpretation in December 2022 that excluded his first period in office from the calculation. 
 Check Out: Chiefs Newcomer Mokwana Closing In On Match Readiness 
 Auf der Heyde has now written to FIFA's Governance, Audit and Compliance Committee requesting an urgent ruling on the matter. With the nomination deadline approaching on 18 November, he has also called for it to be suspended until the eligibility question is resolved. 
 "FIFA should not allow the nomination deadline to expire while there is an unresolved question about whether the incumbent is entitled to stand," he said. 
 He has requested a response by 16 November and appealed to all 211 member associations to support his call for a formal ruling, insisting that the issue is about FIFA's responsibility to apply its own rules. 
 Not an Elections Issue, but an Infantino One 
 Auf der Heyde says his campaign is not driven by personal ambition and that he would step aside if a more suitable challenger emerged. He has also indicated that he would withdraw should Infantino be ruled ineligible. 
 Check Out: Ronaldinho ‘Open’ To Continue After Return To Football  
 "I entered this campaign because I believed that Infantino needed to be challenged and that FIFA should not have an uncontested presidential election. 
 "If a more suitable candidate comes forward who is prepared to challenge Infantino and offer football a genuine alternative, I will not seek election. 
 "Equally, if Infantino is ruled ineligible, I will withdraw my candidacy." 
 Auf der Heyde previously served as sports editor of the German Press Agency (dpa), edited South Africa's Soccer News and has undertaken professional assignments for FIFA and FIFPRO. He is currently a university lecturer at Southampton Solent University.
